articles.title: Connor McDavid is off to a historic start. Could some of Gretzky's records fall this season?
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid is known for his blistering speed — and so far this year he's also flying up the stats leaderboard at a pace not seen since the days of Wayne Gretzky and Mario…

image.caption: Edmonton Oilers centre Connor McDavid in Dallas in May. Early in the 2026-27 NHL season, McDavid is on pace to challenge individual seasons by legends such as Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux. (Gareth Patterson/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New

Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid is known for his blistering speed — and so far this year he's also flying up the stats leaderboard at a pace not seen since the days of Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux.
In early going, McDavid playing at a pace worthy — or better — than all-time greats

"You just really run out of words," his linemate Leon Draisaitl said after a 6-5 win over the usually stingy Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, during which McDavid picked up his third five-point game of the young season.

McDavid, 29, has always been elite: after an injury-marred rookie season in 2015-16, the centre has been among the league's top scorers ever since, claiming the top spot six times, tying Lemieux and Gordie Howe and trailing only Gretzky (get used to reading that).

But so far in his 12th season he's taken it to another level. It's still very early — just 10 games into an 84-game season. But McDavid's start has hockey fans and players at least asking questions about what No. 97 might be able to accomplish this season.
What McDavid has done so far
First, the straight stat line: McDavid has eight goals and 23 assists in 10 games.

How good is that? Well, he's 10 points ahead of his closest competitor, his own linemate Leon Draisaitl. The next closest player, one not getting passes directly from McDavid, is Vegas Golden Knight Jack Eichel, who has 19 points and has also played two more games than McDavid.

items: Edmonton Oilers name Mike Babcock as coach after hire cleared by NHL
Oilers' superstar captain Connor McDavid wins 5th Ted Lindsay Award, tying Gretzky

blocks.text: McDavid has more assists than anyone else in the league has points. And the vast majority of his assists are "real." In hockey, you get what's known as a secondary assist if you deliver the pass before the pass that leads to the goal.
Of McDavid's 23 assists, only five are secondary assists, according to statistics site Moneypuck. His 18 primary assists are double the next closest player, New York Rangers defenceman Adam Fox.
Historic pace
Now, the pace.

McDavid's start is record-breaking (and maybe unsustainable). McDavid is only the fourth player in league history to hit the 30-point mark in 10 games, along with New York Islanders sniper Mike Bossy, Lemieux (who did it in fewer) and, yes, Gretzky.
Whether McDavid can keep this pace up promises to be a throughline for the rest of the season:

items: Could McDavid become the fastest player to reach 100 points in a season? Gretzky did it in 34 games in 1983-84, which would mean McDavid would need to keep this up until the second week of December.
Could he be the first player since Gretzky to score 200 points in a season? He'd also be the only player other than Gretzky, who did it four times.

Could he even break Gretzky's single-season record of 215 points in 1985-86? In a league where teams score roughly one goal fewer per game than 40 years ago (3.08 now vs. 3.97 then, says hockey-reference.com), McDavid is currently on pace for 260 points. If he kept this pace, he'd surpass Gretzky's season assists record by about 30 assists.

blocks.text: It's also worth noting that on his current pace he'd still beat Gretzky's records even if he only played 80 games, which was the season length for most of The Great One's career.
To break into the top 10 seasons of all time, which would be less historic but still impressive, McDavid would need at least 165 points to slip ahead of Gretzky's 1980-81 season.
Gretzky has eight of the top 10 seasons; Lemieux has two.
McDavid celebrates an Oilers goal in L.A. on Oct. 13. (Luke Hales/Getty Images)
It's a tall order, but McDavid's teammates don't think he's reached his pinnacle yet.

"You learn, right?" Draisaitl said. "When he was 24 he was just as flashy, just as fast, but there's little details that maybe weren't as great. Now his game is as complete as it gets and he hasn't lost a step offensively."
McDavid's next game is against the Toronto Maple Leafs in Edmonton on Saturday.

articles.title: PCG drives away foreign fishing vessel from Lawak Island
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) drove away a foreign fishing vessel from the territorial sea of Lawak Island in the Kalayaan Island Group on Friday.

blocks.text: Published October 24, 2026 2:06am
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) drove away a foreign fishing vessel from the territorial sea of Lawak Island in the Kalayaan Island Group on Friday.

PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea (WPS) Commodore Jay Tarriela said PCG personnel stationed on the island spotted the vessel around noon, approximately two nautical miles northeast of Lawak Island and within its 12-nautical-mile territorial sea.
In the early afternoon, the Coast Guard deployed a rubber boat to conduct maritime patrol and law enforcement operations and order the Vietnamese-flagged vessel to leave the area.
Upon reaching the vessel, PCG personnel issued repeated radio challenges and verbal warnings.
The vessel eventually started its engine and sailed northward, away from the island.
The PCG team then escorted the vessel at a safe distance while continuing to issue radio challenges and warnings until it had left Lawak Island's territorial sea.

"Lawak Island is an integral part of the Municipality of Kalayaan, Province of Palawan. Under international law, the Philippines exercises full sovereignty over its territorial sea, where no foreign vessel may fish without authorization. Such activities likewise constitute violations of Philippine laws, including the Philippine Fisheries Code and the Philippine Maritime Zones Act," Tarriela said. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: US and Israel are warned against launching fresh strikes on Iran
articles.summary:
Multinational ‘anti-war bloc’ uses Istanbul summit to call for a diplomatic solution to Middle East crisis

Foreign ministers at a summit of eight European and Middle Eastern countries have…

blocks.text: Foreign ministers at a summit of eight European and Middle Eastern countries have urged the US and Israel not to renews their attacks on Iran, warning a fresh outbreak of fighting would spread conflict and push oil prices even higher.

The development of a new multinational “anti-war bloc” represents a challenge to the increasingly open plans by the US and Israel to relaunch strikes on Iran while talks on Tehran’s nuclear programme remain deadlocked.

The Turkish foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, joint convener of the summit in Istanbul, said: “Military intervention in Iran is not any kind of solution. We agreed that a new military attack would spread the war and the conflict in the region. All the countries around the table do not want the war to spread even more, once again.”
Ministers also demanded an end to the Houthi assaults on Saudi Arabia, and an immediate opening of the strait of Hormuz currently blockaded by Iranian ships and drones.

Jean-Noël Barrot, the French foreign minister, said another war between Iran and the US would be bad for both sides, and only worsen rising oil prices, which have hit their highest level since May. Ed Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, also urged both sides to embrace diplomacy.

The Istanbul meeting, an unprecedented gathering of regional and European leaders initiated by Turkey and Germany, represented a rare chance for European ministers to have any input into the crises afflicting the Middle East, including in Yemen, Palestine and Iran. They have largely been left as bystanders, apart from sending air force protection to Saudi Arabia as it tries to fend off Houthi drone and missile assaults on its airports and energy installations.

The Middle Eastern states were represented by Fidan, Egypt’s Badr Abdelatty, Pakistan’s Ishaq Dar and Saudi Arabia’s Faisal bin Farhan. Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia formed the Mecca defensive security pact in August, a grouping Egypt may join.

The European side was represented by Barrot, Miliband, Germany’s Johann Wadephul and Italy’s Antonio Tajani. The agenda covered the Palestinian issue, including settlement expansion, settler violence and the two-state solution, as well as security in the strait of Hormuz, Yemen and efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war and prevent spillover into the Black Sea.
Wadephul said: “We are united by the impact these deadlocked conflicts are having on the economy and security of our countries and by the will to seek new ways to bring about solutions.”
He made no criticism of the US but accused “the Houthis and Iran of blackmailing world trade and continuing to stranglehold global supplies of energy and fertiliser”.
“We are feeling the effects of the attacks on shipping routes and whether at the petrol pump or the supermarket,” he said. “Elsewhere there is threat of famine.”
Tajani said the aim of the meeting was to work for “de-escalation to guarantee freedom of navigation”.

“I do not believe the problem can be solved from a purely military standpoint,” he added. “If we want to reopen Hormuz, which is vital for our economies, we must promote dialogue and make Iran understand that this attitude cannot continue.”

articles.title: UK children just as likely to have suffered harm on social media despite crackdown
articles.summary:
Campaigners call lack of progress ‘staggering’, as Ofcom also admits little change in severity of harm to children encountering unsafe content

Landmark online safety measures have failed to…

blocks.text: Landmark online safety measures have failed to limit the proportion of children suffering harm from social media, the UK’s online regulator has admitted, in an assessment branded “staggering” by campaigners.

The proportion of children being fed unsafe content that often left them frightened, confused and upset, was almost unchanged, according to an Ofcom review of the first nine months of supposedly strict requirements on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.

Under the Online Safety Act, the tech giants had to protect children from harmful content including pornography, serious violence, suicide material, racism, misogyny and bullying, with a series of specific duties introduced in summer 2025.

But Ofcom found that “at a total level there was no significant change in the proportion of children encountering harmful content over the first nine months after the children’s safety duties came into force in July 2025”.
It called the finding “concerning” and said there was no evidence indicating a change in the severity of harm since the flagship regulations, under the Online Safety Act, took effect.

Examples of harms included children being shown the murder of Charlie Kirk, graphic pornography and weapon-related content making them feel unsafe in their schools and neighbourhoods. Personalised recommendation feeds powered by “for you” algorithms were repeatedly found by Ofcom to be at the root of the continuing tide of harmful material.

The findings come a week after a coroner concluded that access to the suicide-related material on TikTok may have played a significant part in the decision of Adriana Retyte, a 14-year-old pupil at Langley school in Norfolk, to take her own life in May.

They come a day after Clavicular, 20, a popular social media influencer who promotes surgery and drugs as part of extreme male beauty regimes and has appeared with Andrew Tate, pleaded not guilty to rape in a US court, raising fresh concerns about the influence of “manosphere” content creators.

Ofcom’s research included tracking the exposure of UK children aged eight to 17 to harmful content on user-to-user services, its impact and their use of safety tools and an analysis of children’s wellbeing after exposure to harmful content. The assessment has been shared with Lisa Nandy, the secretary of state for digital, culture, media and sport.

NSPCC, a child protection charity, said the findings showed that children were being exposed to harmful content at an “alarming rate”, which it said was echoed in the flow of calls for help to Childline, its online and telephone support service. Rani Govender, the head of child safety online, said “progress is not happening nearly fast enough”.

“Tech companies have had months to act, yet too many platforms are still built to keep children hooked with their algorithms continuing to push harmful content to their young users,” she said. “We urgently need stronger action from tech companies to rein in features that drive harm to children and stop putting business interests over their safety obligations.”

Dame Melanie Dawes, the watchdog’s chief executive, this week told MPs: “We do not see a safety culture from these large social media companies.” The regulator is already facing a wave of legal actions from tech companies challenging its powers including the Instagram operator Meta, as well as TikTok and X, owned by Elon Musk’s SpaceX group. It has warned it risks being “absolutely clobbered legally by deep-pocketed individuals and firms”.

Children most commonly reported encountering pornographic content via personalised feeds, and girls, in particular, reported feeling confused or upset after seeing such content, Ofcom found. Suicide and eating disorder content was also driven mostly through personal feeds, with girls most likely to encounter both types of harmful material. The Ofcom review also found that “young men and boys consuming motivational and self-improvement content can rapidly become exposed to more extreme content which includes the promotion of misogyny and racism”. Misspelled hashtags and coded language are often used to bypass content moderation systems that would otherwise block harmful misogynistic content.

Ian Russell, the father of Molly Russell, who took her life aged 14 in 2017 after viewing suicide material on social media, told the Guardian the lack of progress was “staggering but sadly not surprising”. He blamed “timidity and lack of action” from the regulator and said: “It is time that Ofcom stood up for children and investigated the major flaws in TikTok and Instagram’s design features, not just small technicalities that have been their focus so far.”

An Ofcom spokesperson said: “This is an industry that’s been unregulated and unaccountable for more than 20 years. And so while significant progress is being made – including the introduction of widespread age checks, stronger protections against grooming, and tougher safeguards against child sexual exploitation and abuse – we’re under no illusion that there is much for the industry still to do. We’ve shown that tech firms that don’t comply with their duties can expect enforcement action.”

It said the data did not cover the period from this spring when it said it stepped up pressure on Facebook, YouTube, Snap, Roblox and TikTok over child safety issues. It also said it recorded some reductions in harmful content on platforms including the games Minecraft and Call of Duty and YouTube, Pinterest and Facebook. In July it launched an investigation into TikTok over child safety concerns, including how it checks users are adults or children.

The continuing risks to children come before a planned Australia-style social media ban in the UK for under-16s which is due, from next spring, to cover platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, Facebook and X, but not messaging services such as WhatsApp and Signal.
However campaigners have warned that must not overshadow the need to enforce protections under the Online Safety Act.

“Children will continue to face risks on services covered by the act but not the proposed ban, including gaming and messaging platforms,” said Mitali Sud, a senior policy manager at Internet Matters, a child online safety campaign. “Sixteen- and 17-year-olds will still use social media. A social media ban cannot replace the need to make online services safer for children.”
A government spokesperson said platforms needed to do more to protect children from harmful content.

“That’s why we are taking bold action to strengthen protections for children from risks of harm online – banning social media from offering their services to under-16s and protecting kids from harmful functionalities like livestreaming and stranger communications on a wide range of services, including gaming services,” they said.

“When it comes to children’s safety, we are not and never will be bystanders. Platforms have both a moral and legal duty to protect children and we expect them to work with us to set a new normal for future generations.”
TikTok, Meta, X and Google were contacted for comment.

articles.title: MapQuest now showing surveillance camera locations across Canada, U.S.
articles.summary: MapQuest users in Canada and the U.S. can now see where some surveillance cameras have been set up in their communities.

image.caption: A screenshot of the MapQuest app shows several eyes marking surveillance cameras in Toronto on Thursday. (CBC)

blocks.text: News·New
MapQuest users in Canada and the U.S. can now see where some surveillance cameras have been set up in their communities.
Users wanted to know where police had set up licence plate readers, company says
The company introduced a "surveillance layer" earlier this week that uses animated eyes to mark where automated licence plate readers, or ALPRs, have been set up by police or others.

"We knew that there were a ton of cameras in use and documented in the U.S. and Canada," MapQuest general manager Doug Berger told CBC News. "You would never know unless they were pointed out to you."

The U.S.-based online mapping service recently went viral, three decades after it launched, after refusing to change the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" following U.S. President Donald Trump's executive order demanding the switch. (Apple and Google changed the lake's name for U.S. users.)
Some three million people in the U.S. and Canada downloaded the app following the move, according to Berger.
"The coolest part of that experience was people were — and still today people are — telling us exactly what they want," he said.
One of the requests was to be able to see surveillance camera locations, he said.
MapQuest's Doug Berger on the app's new found popularity after standing strong on Lake Ontario name
Police have maintained that ALPRs are an effective tool for identifying criminals, stolen vehicles and missing persons, and that most data is quickly deleted.
The data is "used solely for law enforcement purposes by authorized personnel only," according to the Toronto Police Service, for example.
But a recent CBC News report found that the growing popularity of ALPRs, especially in the U.S., has raised privacy concerns.

"There are concerns of misuse," the Canadian Civil Liberties Association's Tamir Israel said in August. "It's been documented in the U.S. that these cameras have been misused by police officers to follow ex-partners around and that kind of thing."

The map markings include cameras set up by Flock, the private company whose ALPRs have stirred controversy and vandalism across the U.S. Other companies behind public cameras include Genetec, PlateSmart, Neology and Verkada.
Berger says highlighting ALPR locations is about transparency.

"We're not taking a political stance against the efficacy of them or anything, but we are bringing forth the visibility of them for people using the MapQuest app in an effort to be transparent," he said.
Camera locations are indicated on the MapQuest mobile app, which is only available to Canadian and U.S. users. The locations are based on open crowd-sourced data from OpenStreetMap.
The locations of licence plate readers like this one in Cornwall, P.E.I., are crowd-sourced data from OpenStreetMap. (CBC)
'Strong visual'

In the app, an icon in the map's lower right corner symbolizes the layers, with one square on top of another. By tapping the icon, a user can select the "surveillance" feature. Within seconds, eyes that shift side to side pop on the screen.
"Our team had a lot of fun with that," Berger said, adding that the eye fit with a few additional Halloween-themed launches.

"The moving eye was spooky and fit nicely with the theme of the Halloween release," Berger said. "At the moment, we don't see a reason to change it. It gives a good strong visual to go along with the fact that there are cameras."
As for the sheer number of eyes that pop up in various neighbourhoods: "It's pretty crazy," Berger said.

items: Côte Saint-Luc, Que., piloting automated licence plate reader cameras
Sudbury police adding new recruits, licence plate scanners
Police cameras may capture licence plates: P.E.I. privacy commissioner

blocks.text: Berger encourages users to keep reaching out with additional requests. For example, new users have also asked the Los Angeles-based company to mark polling locations during elections. The company is trying to do that ahead of the U.S. midterms next month.
It hopes to launch a similar feature in Canada for future elections, too, he says.
"It's very consistent with our belief in transparency," Berger said. "It just makes so much sense in a map context."
AI-powered surveillance cameras are spreading in Canada
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Anya Zoledziowski is a Peabody-winning multimedia journalist from Edmonton who's covered social and climate justice, Indigenous affairs, gender, politics and more, and has been recognized by several national and international awards. She’s currently pursuing her PhD in journalism studies.

articles.title: Tommy Robinson guilty of harassment because this is not a vigilante world, jury told
articles.summary:
Prosecution says Robinson ‘threatened people and acted like a bully’ towards Daily Mail journalists

Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a…

blocks.text: Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a “vigilante world”, jurors have been told, as the prosecution sought to use the far-right activist’s words against him.

Robinson had posted a video in which he told Daily Mail journalists he would find them after they wrote about his alleged role influencing England’s 2024 riots. He told them he had obtained details of where they and their families lived and warned them to abide by “men’s rules”.

Ben Holt, prosecuting, told the jury: “Let’s get real, shall we, and not live in a vigilante world where ‘men’s rules’ apply? Whatever they are. Let’s ground ourselves in a country where there is law and order.”

Summing up the case, Holt said Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, had accepted that sharing images of journalists’ homes and partial photos of their loved ones was intended to exert pressure.

However, he rejected Robinson’s insistence that the journalists on the receiving end of what the prosecution described as “bullyboy and intimidatory” conduct would not have been in fear of violence as a result.
Robinson, 43, is charged with two counts of harassment causing fear of violence in 2024 to two journalists who were working for the Mail, Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber. He denies the charges.

Robinson said in evidence that he had been in “a panic” after the Mail had in effect identified a hotel in Cyprus where he had gone with family and friends and published a photo of his ex-wife, which he said put her at risk.

But Holt said Robinson had never asked for the image to be taken down in calls and messages to the journalists and the Daily Mail’s editor. “Instead, he just threatened people. He acted like a bully,” he said.

Holt repeated the words Robinson had directed at the journalists: “Good for the goose, good for the gander. You are coming for me, I am coming for you.” Holt described this as “straightforward retaliation”.

Such was the concern of the journalists that the police had to be called on a number of occasions, said Holt, who pointed to “unpleasant” comments made by Robinson’s supporters online after some of his posts. Robinson had close to 1 million followers on X at point, and some of his supporters are “unpredictable”, Holt said.
Alisdair Williamson KC, for the defence, said Robinson’s actions were justified because the “fear for him is real”.

“When you judge whether what he did was reasonable, you might think that he showed some restraint,” he told the jury. “I know what language I might use if people put my family in that position. The fear for him is real.”
Williamson said the journalists did not care about Robinson’s issues with the article, nor the stress it caused him, adding: “They don’t care to pick up the phone.”

A series of agreed facts that were read out to the court before the closing speeches included a reference to four threat-to-life warning notices that police had given to Robinson in 2018, 2019 and 2024, shortly after the Daily Mail article.

The court also heard that a video had been posted online in August 2024 by a man named Omar Abdirizak in which he said: “Tommy Robinson I got a message for you … we got pirates in every corner. Muslims in every corner,” before making a rifle gesture.
The trial continues.

articles.title: Opposition deepfake video sparks outrage in Spain ahead of election
articles.summary:
Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing

A political ad from Spain’s main opposition party that used a deepfake video of…

blocks.text: A political ad from Spain’s main opposition party that used a deepfake video of the prime minister’s wife has sparked outrage and set off a wider debate on AI, as the deeply polarised country gears up for general elections next month.

Launched this week across the social media channels of the conservative People’s party (PP), the video used artificial intelligence to manipulate the likenesses of various people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party and appeared to show them admitting to acts such as soliciting prostitutes and taking kickbacks.

An AI-generated version of Sánchez’s wife, Begoña Gómez, for example, speaks about receiving a university post thanks to her husband’s job, while a deepfake of the former Socialist president José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero speaks about hiding jewellery in a safe. Both lines are nods to ongoing investigations in which Gómez and Zapatero have denied any wrongdoing.

blocks.caption: A still from the People’s party AI-generated video featuring a deepfake of Begoña Gomez. Computer-generated: @ppopular/X

blocks.text: The Socialist party was swift to respond to the video, which by Friday had racked up nearly 2m views. “It’s telling people a colossal lie, and for a party to do it on its official accounts seems intolerable to me,” Óscar López, Spain’s digital transformation minister, told the broadcaster TVE on Friday.

While the video noted at the bottom – in tiny, nearly transparent font – that it had been created with AI, López pointed to the wider risk. “It’s very easy for anyone who isn’t used to AI to confuse that video with reality,” he said. “And call me crazy, but that seems extremely serious to me.”

On Friday, one of those whose likeness was used in the video filed a legal challenge against the PP, calling on the party to immediately take down the campaign advert. In a court complaint, Leire Díez, a former Socialist party member, reportedly accused the PP of defamation and digital identity theft, after the video used her likeness to hint at accusations that she worked to undermine judicial and law enforcement in order to help the Socialists.

A majority of the nine legal experts consulted by the newspaper El País concurred that what the PP had done was not illegal, given that the video was labelled as AI-generated and that the overall tone was one of political satire. “Given the context, everyone knows those people didn’t say those things,” Íñigo Navarro, a former dean of the faculty of law at Madrid’s Comillas Pontifical University, told the paper.

But the legality of the video was just one aspect, said Juan Antonio Lascuraín, a professor of criminal law at the Autonomous University of Madrid. “It’s quite another matter to ask whether it’s appropriate, exemplary or ethically and politically correct.”
Many sought to contextualise the videos within the wider effort – under way by officials across much of the world – to crack down on the impact of disinformation.

“It’s truly regrettable that the official account of a party that claims to want to govern and revitalise democracy is using AI-generated deepfakes in its campaign,” said José Javier Olivas, an associate professor who researches populism, conspiracy theories and AI biases at Spain’s National University for Distance Education.

He pointed to the wider backdrop of the election campaign, in which both mainstream parties have sought to rally voters by stoking emotions and attacking the morality of their rivals, but he said the video was a “red line” in terms of how campaigns normally unfolded.
after newsletter promotion
“You’re using the images of other people, putting words in their mouths that they’re not saying, [and] this qualifies for disinformation,” he said.

The use of AI to generate or enhance political ads has also become a talking point in the US ahead of next month’s midterm elections. A recent report by a research group based at Wesleyan University in Connecticut identified more than 200 such ads, the vast majority of them tied to the Republicans.

“AI is making its way into the 2026 midterms in a big way this year,” said Erika Franklin Fowler, a co-director of the Wesleyan Media Project. “For comparison, we identified less than $50,000 in spending on AI-generated ads in the 2024 cycle. Much of the AI use is not disclosed through any type of disclaimer.”

In Spain, the PP has brushed off criticism. “If there had been malicious intent to make people believe that the characters who appear there are real, then we’d have a problem,” Borja Sémper, of the party, told reporters. “But everyone can see that this is a way of using digital tools to highlight the hypocrisy in which the Socialist party operates.”
Most polls suggest the PP will win the 29 November general election but will need to rely on the support of the far-right Vox party to form a government.

articles.title: The saga is over as Winnipeg Jets trade Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey
articles.summary: The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg after the Jets traded the all-star goalie on Friday.

image.caption: Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, seen in a file photo from April 2026, made his debut with the team in November 2015. He won three Vezina trophies as the NHL's top goaltender with the Jets. (Tony Gutierrez/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Breaking
The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg after the Jets traded the all-star goalie on Friday.
3-time Vezina-winning goalie told team at the end of last season that he wanted out
The 33-year-old from Michigan is headed to the New Jersey Devils.

In return, the Jets acquire forwards Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command, Nick Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, and New Jersey’s second-round pick in the 2029 NHL draft and seventh-round pick in the 2027 draft.
The Jets are set to host the Devils at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg on Nov. 10.
Hellebuyck is a three-time Vezina Trophy winner and 2025 Hart Trophy winner as NHL MVP who has made five appearances at the NHL All-Star Game.
He also backstopped the U.S. men's hockey team to an Olympic gold medal in February 2026.

He still had five years left on a seven-year contract but told the team during exit interviews at the end of last season that he wanted to be moved, general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff told reporters last month.

items: Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck goes public with trade request
Winnipeg Jets suspend star goalie Connor Hellebuyck for failing to report to training camp

blocks.text: There was speculation it was because Hellebuyck and his family were targets of online harassment after the goalie and some Olympic teammates visited the White House.

U.S. President Donald Trump gave Hellebuyck the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the U.S.'s highest civilian honour, while anti-American sentiment was soaring in Canada due to Trump's tariffs and references to making Canada the 51st state.

Cheveldayoff told reporters in September that the harassment had escalated to the point where team security and local police were involved, with increased monitoring around Hellebuyck's Winnipeg residence.
Others speculated Hellebuyck's trade demands were prompted by the Jets' poor performance last season.
When the Jets re-signed him in 2023, it was seen as a commitment to build a squad that would consistently compete for the Stanley Cup.

items: Jets' coach Arniel stickhandles around Hellebuyck's status as suspension end looms
Jets waiting to 'get this right,' not rushing to trade star goalie Connor Hellebuyck

blocks.text: Then the Jets missed the playoffs in 2025-26 for the first time in four seasons after winning the President's Trophy for the league's best regular-season record in 2024-25.
Hellebuyck voiced strong frustration.
"What we did was unacceptable, and no one wants to be a part of that," he said.
Cheveldayoff said last month that the team was respecting Hellebuyck’s request to keep the trade request quiet and was caught off guard when Hellebuyck went public on Aug. 27.
When he was a no-show for training camp in September, the Jets suspended him.
Hellebuyck notified the team on Oct. 2 that he planned to end his absence, but the Jets chose to enforce the full three-week suspension rather than immediately reintegrate him.
That suspension was set to expire on Friday.
Cheveldayoff last month said he was in no rush to make a trade, choosing instead to wait for the right offer.
He told reporters he didn’t want "future assets" that may or may not work out. He wanted players who could offer immediate production to support those who had committed to the team.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Darren Bernhardt has been with CBC Manitoba since 2009 and specializes in offbeat and local history stories. He is the author of two bestselling books: The Lesser Known: A History of Oddities from the Heart of the Continent, and Prairie Oddities: Punkinhead, Peculiar Gravity and More Lesser Known Histories.

articles.title: Thousands of homes without power as Storm Austen hits south-west England
articles.summary:
Dozens of schools in Cornwall also affected as another storm heads for Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England

Thousands of homes are without power and schools were closed as the…

blocks.text: Thousands of homes are without power and schools were closed as the first named storm of the year hit UK shores.

Storm Austen brought severe conditions to parts of the south-west, with a gust of 76mph recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly on Friday morning. Just before 11am, more than 16,000 homes in the south-west were without power, according to National Grid.

Dozens of schools across Cornwall were forced to open late, while others did not open at all. Flights were disrupted at airports in the south-west and on the Channel Islands, and passengers were being advised to check the status of their flight before travelling.

Guernsey airport’s duty manager, Steve Ford, confirmed that normal service was not expected to resume before Saturday morning, with most of the fleet having been stranded on the UK mainland. The Dutch flag carrier, KLM, cancelled dozens of its scheduled flights for Friday and Saturday.

Images showed part of Brighton’s West Pier falling into the sea after it was battered by wind and waves. The pier, first opened in 1866, has grown increasingly derelict since it closed to the public in 1975, with storms and fires destroying much of what remained. English Heritage has previously declared the structure beyond repair.
National Rail reported severe disruption across the rail network, with cancellations across England, Wales and Scotland.
Forecasters have put an additional amber weather warning for wind in place from Saturday into Sunday as the second named storm of the year, Boelo, heads in.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, said: “We potentially are facing a winter of greater flooding, so it’s about recognising all of those risks and taking action.”

blocks.caption: Andy Burnham speaking at a wildfires summit in Aintree, Liverpool, on Friday. Photograph: WPA/Getty

blocks.text: A government campaign aimed at urging people to stock supplies of food and essentials in case of multi-day emergencies made headlines overnight. Burnham was asked whether the government was playing catch-up with civil preparedness as he attended a summit organised to learn from the summer’s record wildfires.
He answered: “No. We are having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we’re living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common.

“We’re in a situation today where the UK is facing storms, and obviously we feel for the people without power in Cornwall right now. It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments [and] we are having that conversation about resilience. That’s why we’re holding this summit today, it’s why we’re putting the guidance out to the public.”
National Grid said engineers had restored power to more than 12,000 properties affected by Storm Austen by 8am on Friday.
after newsletter promotion
A Met Office amber warning for wind covering Cornwall, Devon and the Isles of Scilly was issued on Wednesday, taking effect on Friday from 1am until 10am.

blocks.caption: Storm Austen hits Newhaven in East Sussex. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

blocks.text: The Met Office has now issued a 24-hour amber warning for wind from Storm Boelo from 9pm on Saturday, covering Scotland, the north coast of Northern Ireland, and Cumbria and Northumberland in the north of England.
The forecaster said gusts of up to 80mph could hit exposed coastal areas, with winds of 60-70mph widespread elsewhere, and it warned of danger to life from flying debris.
It said there was also a “good chance” of power cuts, damage to buildings, trees being uprooted and rail and flight cancellations.
The Republic of Ireland’s weather agency, Met Éireann, issued six warnings of varying severity for Saturday, mostly affecting counties along the west coast.

articles.title: Sherwin: Recall of House budget bill unnecessary
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday rejected calls from the Makabayan bloc in the House of Representatives to recall the chamber’s budget bill for 2027, saying that the Senate would…

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator Sherwin Gatchalian..
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday rejected calls from the Makabayan bloc in the House of Representatives to recall the chamber’s budget bill for 2027, saying that the Senate would make the necessary corrections to ensure constitutional compliance without risking a reenacted budget.

House Deputy Minority Leader Antonio Tinio and his Makabayan colleagues recently urged Congress to pull the House-approved version of the 2027 budget from the Senate, arguing that it contains provisions that mirror elements struck down by the Supreme Court, including questionable triggers for unprogrammed appropriations and prohibited lump-sum allocations.

“I think it’s important and necessary so that the House can clean up its own mess, because if you look at the budget passed by the House, there are significant parts that could be declared unconstitutional as well,” Tinio explained. “We don’t want yet another budget that will be declared unconstitutional.”
However, Gatchalian dismissed the necessity of recall, explaining that the Senate is already positioned to correct these flaws during its consolidation and committee report process.
“Not necessary because we are entering the consolidation of the budget here so we can do the correction ourselves,” Gatchalian told reporters.

“Rest assured, the 2027 budget will be compliant with [the] Constitution,” Gatchalian said, adding that the 2027 budget would not mirror the unconstitutional provisions flagged by the high court in the 2024 and 2025 budgets.

Meanwhile, Sen. Panfilo Lacson warned that returning the budget bill to the House would likely result in a reenacted budget – a scenario that he described as “worse” because it operates on lump sums without itemized provisions.
“That is not the solution. The solution is for the Senate to really scrutinize and cut all the fat sent in the GAB [General Appropriations Bill] of the House. That is the solution,” Lacson said.
He suggested Makabayan bloc lawmakers should instead raise their concerns with their House colleagues who would eventually sit in the bicameral conference committee.
Senate budget
In a bid to set an example for fiscal discipline, Lacson revealed that the Senate plans to slash its own proposed budget by P2 billion.

“In fact, we agreed with the Senate President the other day, me being the chairman of the committee on accounts, we will reduce our budget, the Senate budget, by about P2 billion from the NEP [National Expenditure Program],” Lacson disclosed.
He pointed out the contrast between the two chambers, noting that while the House added P5 billion to its own allocation, the Senate is taking the opposite route.

Lacson gave assurance that the P2-billion cut – which will bring the Senate’s budget down to P5 billion from the proposed P7 billion – will not disrupt the chamber’s operations, as there are still unused funds available.

Gatchalian said the Senate is also addressing red flags in the House version, particularly concerning infrastructure insertions, with some farm-to-market road projects proposed by the House having been plotted in the middle of the ocean.
“There are coordinates there that is in the Benham Rise or in the Middle East. So we have to check. I’m sure it’s a typo,” Gatchalian said.
The Senate President added they have already flagged the Department of Agriculture regarding these errors and duplicate project entries.
Lacson noted that the Senate’s decision to invite civil society organizations as resource persons during the budget hearings has been instrumental in exposing these anomalies. – Delon Porcalla

articles.title: Diesel price hike looms; rollback for gasoline
articles.summary: Motorists should brace for another increase in diesel prices next week as escalating hostilities in the Middle East threaten to further disrupt global oil supplies.

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Motorists should brace for another increase in diesel prices next week as escalating hostilities in the Middle East threaten to further disrupt global oil supplies.

Based on the first four days of trading in the Mean of Platts Singapore, the regional benchmark for refined petroleum products in the Asia-Pacific, diesel prices are projected to rise by P2 to P2.50 per liter.
Gasoline prices, meanwhile, could drop by P1 to P1.50 per liter.
The projected adjustments remain preliminary as they do not yet account for week-on-week changes in freight costs.
Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said oil prices rallied amid mounting supply concerns following intensified Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and vessels.
“Loadings outside of the Arab Gulf are now threatened as well, jeopardizing Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that helped support regional loadings,” Bellas said.
Market anxiety has also been fueled by fears of further escalation in geopolitical tensions following the US midterm elections.
For refined petroleum products, diesel prices have come under additional upward pressure from declining oil flows and intensified Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.
“Meanwhile, rising gasoline inventories in Singapore pointed to an improving product availability in Asia,” Bellas said.
He added that persistent tightness in diesel supplies has encouraged refiners to maintain crude processing rates, potentially helping sustain gasoline supply even as demand weakens.
The Department of Energy is expected to announce the prescribed pump price adjustments on Monday.
Strategic oil reserves

Amid continuing oil price volatility, lawmakers are pushing for the creation of a Philippine Strategic Petroleum Reserve System to help shield consumers and businesses from supply disruptions and sharp price increases.
Camarines Sur Reps. Migz Villafuerte and Luigi Villafuerte urged yesterday their colleagues in the House of Representatives to support House Bill 9367, which seeks to establish the reserve system.
The measure was also authored by Rep. Tsuyoshi Anthony Horibata and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon.
The lawmakers explained that the country’s dependence on imported petroleum products leaves it vulnerable to global market fluctuations, underscoring the need for government-controlled fuel reserves.

“Despite its heavy reliance on imported petroleum products, our country lacks a comprehensive legal framework establishing a government-controlled strategic petroleum reserve that will protect Filipinos and businesses from wild swings in the prices of diesel, gasoline and other petroleum products,” Luigi said.
Migz, meanwhile, noted that countries with established strategic petroleum reserves could draw on their stocks during supply disruptions and periods of severe price volatility.

“The Philippines has no comparable government-controlled strategic petroleum reserve to draw from during a major supply disruption and thus remains largely exposed to market volatility, relying instead on commercial inventories and external supply conditions,” he said.

The proposed framework would cover the acquisition, storage, maintenance, rotation and emergency release of petroleum reserves. It would also allow the Department of Energy to work with private entities through public-private partnerships to develop and operate reserve facilities.

The push for legislation comes as Maharlika Investment Corp. and the Philippine National Oil Co. have signed a memorandum of understanding to evaluate the development, financing and operation of a strategic tank farm in Bataan.
The PNOC is targeting the facility’s operations to begin by 2028, with an initial capacity of one million barrels that could eventually expand to 15 million barrels.
Illegal fuel
Meanwhile, Metro Manila police have intensified operations against illegal fuel trading amid concerns that unscrupulous sellers could exploit supply uncertainties.
Metro Manila police officer-in-charge Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano ordered police intelligence units and station commanders to strengthen monitoring and validation of unauthorized fuel trading.
The directive followed the arrest of four individuals by Quezon City police on Tuesday for allegedly selling 172 liters of petroleum products illegally beside a gasoline station in Payatas.

“While the government is working to ensure a sufficient and stable fuel supply for our country, we will not allow illegal traders to take advantage of the situation for their own gain,” Abrahano said. – Delon Porcalla, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: P50 million bounty up for Bato’s capture
articles.summary: Saying the gloves are off, the government has put up a P50-million bounty for any information that will lead to the capture of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, and gave him a week to…

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Saying the gloves are off, the government has put up a P50-million bounty for any information that will lead to the capture of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, and gave him a week to surrender. In announcing the reward, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the senator, who is considered “armed and dangerous,” has been given all the courtesy to voluntarily surrender following an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant of arrest issued in November 2025.
Dela Rosa, a former Philippine National Police (PNP) chief, has been tagged a co-conspirator of former president Rodrigo Duterte in the crimes against humanity case before the ICC.
Instead of showing up and taking responsibility for his actions, Remulla said Dela Rosa is a coward by remaining in hiding.

“Senator Bato mistook my gesture of negotiation as a sign of weakness. It’s time for the gloves to come off. It’s time to bring justice to his victims,” Remulla told a news briefing at Camp Crame yesterday.
“As of today, Senator Bato will be considered armed and dangerous. We are placing a bounty of P50 million for his capture,” Remulla said.

With the reward, Dela Rosa is now the No. 1 most wanted fugitive in the country, followed by gambling tycoon Charlie “Atong” Ang, who has a P20-million bounty for his arrest in connection with the alleged kidnapping and killing of cockfight enthusiasts or sabungeros.
The bounty for Dela Rosa was sourced from the intelligence funds of the DILG and the PNP, Remulla said.
Remulla has designated PNP deputy chief for administration Lt. Gen. Wilson Lopez as the head of a special task force to arrest Dela Rosa.
PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said Dela Rosa has one week to surrender but maintained law enforcement operations to arrest the senator are ongoing.
Apart from intelligence operatives, Nartatez said they are also utilizing tactical teams and other resources to locate and arrest Dela Rosa.
“With or without ultimatum, with or without reward, the PNP is ready to implement whatever (needs) to be implemented. That is our commitment,” he said.
Dela Rosa is allegedly being protected by a powerful armed group in a secluded area in Mindanao, the reason why Remulla is cautious about launching an operation to arrest the senator by force.
The DILG chief said a bloodbath similar to the siege of Marawi in 2017 could ensue.
For Nartatez, the possibility of casualties is always there but maintained they have contingency measures in place to ensure the lawmaker is caught.
“For example, the coddlers are 10 (people), then we will need a hundred (operatives). It will be a calibrated one,” Nartatez said.

The PNP has searched several areas in Mindanao and Luzon, including Metro Manila, where there have been reported sightings of Dela Rosa but all turned out negative. Nartatez said they could not see a pattern on Dela Rosa’s movements. Nartatez warned Dela Rosa’s coddlers to stop protecting Dela Rosa and hand him over to authorities or face criminal cases.
Dela Rosa’s last public appearance was on May 14, when he was seen exiting the Senate premises alongside Sen. Robinhood Padilla, his colleague in the minority.
Local warrant first
Dela Rosa’s counsel Israelito Torreon rejected the DILG’s bounty for his client, saying a local warrant must first exist.
Torreon’s law firm made a lengthy post on social media yesterday, after the lawyer initially said “no comment” on the matter.
“A reward system built on Philippine warrants cannot be used for a person who has no Philippine warrant,” the law firm of Torreon & Partners posted on Facebook.

“The only document the government has is a warrant from the International Criminal Court. That is a foreign tribunal under a treaty the Philippines withdrew from effective March 17, 2019. No Philippine judge has examined that warrant, adopted it or issued one of his own,” Torreon claimed. – Ghio Ong

articles.title: ICC prosecutor wants more recorded testimonies admitted
articles.summary: The Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court has requested six more prior recorded testimonies of witnesses to be admitted in the crimes against humanity case against former…

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has requested six more prior recorded testimonies of witnesses to be admitted in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

Acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang filed two separate requests seeking the admission of recorded testimonies of witnesses who he said would cover details of Duterte’s drug war, including alleged extrajudicial killings.
This brings the total number of witnesses covered by requests for admission of prior recorded testimonies to 15.
The first of the two new requests, originally filed on Oct. 12, covered witnesses P-0024, P-1357 and P-1359.
Niang said their testimonies primarily relate to the contextual elements of crimes against humanity.
He said their testimonies are suitable for formal submission in written form as they are “cumulative or corroborative nature.”

Based on the filing, P-0024’s written testimony will cover the legal process surrounding the drug war. P-1357 focuses on matters relating to the Davao death squad, while P-1359 discussed the increase in drug-related shooting incidents following Duterte’s election as president.
Meanwhile, the latest set of witnesses were covered in the Oct. 19 filing made public on Oct. 23.
Unlike the previous three, the prosecution still intends to present witnesses P-0008, P-1164 and P- 1303 even if their prior recorded testimonies are accepted by chamber.
The testimonies of P-0008 and P-1164 cover the extrajudicial killings allegedly perpetrated by police in the context of the drug war, including specific incidents included.
Meanwhile, P-1303’s testimony – in addition to covering some specific incidents – also includes general evidence on matters related to drug use.

articles.title: Poll: Only 28% see fair ruling in VP impeachment
articles.summary: Compared to previous impeachment trials, a smaller proportion of Filipinos expect a fair ruling in the ongoing Senate proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, a survey by Social Weather…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte at the 54th Datu Bago Awards Conferment 2026 in Davao City.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebok

MANILA, Philippines — Compared to previous impeachment trials, a smaller proportion of Filipinos expect a fair ruling in the ongoing Senate proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, a survey by Social Weather Stations (SWS) showed.
The poll, conducted from Sept. 21 to 27, found that only 28 percent of the respondents have “much trust” in the Senate that it would make a fair decision in the impeachment trial.

It was lower than the 32 percent obtained in December 2000 during the impeachment trial of then-president Joseph Estrada and the 30 percent obtained in March 2012 during the trial of then Supreme Court chief justice Renato Corona.
At 35 percent, more Filipinos also have little trust now in the Senate to make a fair decision. It was only at 15 percent in December 2000 and 19 percent in March 2012.
Based on the latest survey, only 42 percent of the respondents closely follow Duterte’s impeachment trial.
Twenty-one percent said they were following it “just a little,” while 27 percent said they were not following at all. Nine percent just heard about the trial from the survey.
Asked about the fairness of proceedings, 50 percent said the Senate impeachment court “has the right consideration for both sides.”

Seventeen percent said the court was too liberal with the prosecutors, while 18 percent said it was too liberal for Duterte’s lawyers. Fifteen percent said they do not know or refused to answer the question.

Only 31 percent said the trial was moving at the right pace, while 39 percent said it was “much too slow.” Twenty-percent thought it was “too much in a hurry,” with the remaining seven percent not providing an answer.
The survey was conducted just as the prosecution wrapped up its presentation of evidence.
The House prosecutors on Oct. 13 formally dropped three out of the four Articles of Impeachment, leaving the issue of unexplained wealth as the sole charge against Duterte.
The court resumes session on Nov. 18, with the defense to begin its presentation of evidence.
Ombudsman studies dropped raps vs VP

Meanwhile, the Office of the Ombudsman will “evaluate” the allegations against Vice President Duterte, including alleged anomalies in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and the bribery charge already withdrawn from the impeachment trial against her.

Journalists asked Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla about updates on the turnover of Duterte’s SALN records and the possible referral of the withdrawn Articles of Impeachment, including the bribery charge, to the ombudsman during his visit to Cebu last Thursday.

Earlier this month, the House prosecution panel decided to withdraw the three out of four Articles of Impeachment against Duterte including the charge of bribery to officials of the Department of Education that she previously headed. They noted they may refer the bribery charge to the ombudsman or the Department of Justice for possible investigation.
During the media briefing, Remulla said ombudsman investigators “will be needing sworn statements.”
“We will evaluate it first and we will see if we need sworn statements… we cannot take it just on word na walang people standing up to the facts,” he explained.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) previously announced it has transferred the case buildup over the alleged misdeclarations in Duterte’s SALN to the ombudsman.
According to Remulla, the NBI’s turnover would undergo fact-finding by his office. – Ghio Ong

articles.title: Tighter estate tax amnesty bill pushed in Senate
articles.summary: Senators are pushing to tighten the proposed estate tax amnesty bill to prevent “fake death” inheritance fraud and discourage taxpayers from deliberately dodging their dues in…

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senators are pushing to tighten the proposed estate tax amnesty bill to prevent “fake death” inheritance fraud and discourage taxpayers from deliberately dodging their dues in anticipation of endless government pardons.

During Friday’s hearing of the Senate committee on ways and means, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian warned that granting a fourth estate tax amnesty since 2019 removes the urgency to pay and accidentally incentivizes tax evasion.
“Maybe after we pass this amnesty law and after a few years they won’t pay again because they know there will be another amnesty,” Gatchalian said.

Instead of treating the amnesty as a cure-all, Gatchalian urged the Department of Finance (DOF) to investigate the root causes of non-payment, questioning whether the baseline six-percent amnesty rate remains too expensive for impoverished families trying to transfer small rice fields or rural lands.

Committee chairman Panfilo Lacson, meanwhile, cautioned against proposals to accept barangay certifications in lieu of official Philippine Statistics Authority death certificates for heirs residing in remote areas.
“In very remote areas, they don’t know how to get death certificate. So what happens, (they get) certification of barangay chairman after attestation by two disinterested persons,” Lacson explained.
“To my mind, this is too subjective and it could lead to fake deaths for inheritance.”
To ensure the government actually secures its revenues, Lacson also proposed a stricter cutoff mechanism for the amnesty availment period, which the DOF proposed to end on June 30, 2028.

articles.title: Cyprus: UNCLOS can’t be applied selectively
articles.summary: Cyprus supports the peaceful settlement of disputes and believes that international law cannot be applied “selectively,” Cypriot Foreign Minister Constantinos Kombos said.

MANILA, Philippines — Cyprus supports the peaceful settlement of disputes and believes that international law cannot be applied “selectively,” Cypriot Foreign Minister Constantinos Kombos said.

“Our position on the application of international law, its fundamental principles and the UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea) is a position of principle,” Kombos told The STAR in a recent interview.

“This position stems both from our obligations as a UN member-state and from our firm belief that international law cannot be applied selectively. The same principles must apply to all states. MANILA, Philippines — Amid the decision of the Chinese embassy to prohibit certain officials and personalities from visiting China, close to a hundred student organizations and youth leaders nationwide declared Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan banned from Philippine schools.
In a joint statement, the student and youth groups said that they would not allow educational institutions to become platforms for a foreign aggressor to undermine Philippine sovereignty.

“Our schools must remain spaces for learning, critical inquiry, and the defense of truth, freedom, and national dignity. They must never be used as platforms for intimidation or for advancing narratives that threaten Philippine sovereignty and our territorial integrity,” the statement read.

Akbayan Youth national chairperson Khylla Meneses said Jing should not be welcomed into Philippine schools while China continues to threaten the country and harass Filipino fisherfolk and frontliners in the West Philippine Sea.
The students and youth groups also called on school and university administrations to stand with their students in defending national sovereignty and academic freedom.

Among the schools where student leaders have declared Jing banned are the University of the Philippines in Diliman, UP Cebu, UP Baguio, Ateneo de Manila University, Ateneo de Zamboanga University, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, Polytechnic University of the Philippines, Universidad de Manila, Philippine Normal University, Taguig City University, University of Caloocan City, Arellano University, University of San Carlos, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa, Rizal Technological University, Central Luzon State University, Bulacan State University, Pampanga State University, Holy Angel University, Palawan State University, Cavite State University, Adamson University and Mindanao State University-General Santos City.
What approval?

“The Philippines did not ask for, and does not need anyone’s ‘approval’ to resupply our own troops aboard BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal. The Oct. 21 mission was a sovereign act of the Philippine government inside our own exclusive economic zone,” Tarriela posted on X.

MANILA, Philippines — The government is hastening the completion of projects to minimize the impact of the super El Niño, President Marcos assured the public yesterday as the climate phenomenon is expected to cause drought in many parts of the country until early next year.?

“But now, we are better prepared than we were in 2024. Our dams have higher water levels compared to the start of 2024,” he said during the inauguration of Tugbong Solar Pump Irrigation Project (SPIP) in Barangay Tugbong, Kananga, Leyte.??

He said the government is speeding up the construction of irrigation systems, water impounding facilities and water distribution networks to minimize the impact of prolonged dry spells on agricultural production and household water supply.
Water impounding projects and dams are also being developed to support fish production and generate hydroelectric power, the President added.?
The Tugbong SPIP, one of two solar-powered irrigation projects inaugurated in Leyte, will provide irrigation to 115 hectares of rice fields in Brgys. Tugbong and Sto. Niño in Kananga.?
The other facility, the Guintigui-an Solar Pump Irrigation Project in Ormoc City, will serve 70 hectares of farmland and benefit 87 farmers.?
Marcos said solar-powered irrigation would help farmers save about P20,000 in diesel costs and could increase their planting cycles from two to three per year.?
The Department of Agriculture (DA) is distributing smaller solar-powered water pumps to farmers to further reduce irrigation costs, he said.?
The administration has established around 3,000 solar pump irrigation systems nationwide as part of its efforts to modernize agriculture and improve farmers’ productivity.
The President said irrigation facilities now cover approximately 70 percent of the country’s agricultural land suitable for irrigation.?
TONAY Solar Irrigators Association Inc., with 66 farmer-members, will operate and maintain the Tugbong SPIP.?
State of calamity

Sen. Francis Pangilinan, chair of the committee on agriculture, called for a proactive government response to mounting agricultural damage across five regions.
“I do agree that it is good to declare [a state of calamity] because from all indications it’s a super El Niño,” the DA secretary said, citing forecastsand assessments by climate experts.

For its part, the Department of Health assured the public its hospitals are ready for a worsening El Niño as DOH Assistant Secretary Tagumpay Maniquis said hospitals have no issues on energy and water. – Josiah Antonio, Rhodina Villanueva, Christine Boton

articles.title: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
articles.summary: Satellite images show oil spreading for miles along the coastline, threatening local marine wildlife
articles.byline: Thomas Copeland, Mark Poynting and Tom Spencer

blocks.text: ByThomas Copeland, Mark Poynting and Tom Spencer
BBC Verify
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas.

Satellite images from Monday show the beginnings of the oil spill from a ship matching the location and dimensions of Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran.
The slick of oil had spread more than 35km (22 miles) from the tanker by Wednesday, the satellite imagery showed.
UAE authorities said on Thursday that the incident is affecting beaches near the northern city of Umm Al Quwain and verified video from Friday shows the oil washing ashore, colouring the water black.

blocks.caption: Side-by-side images of the same beach in the northern UAE. The left image, labelled February 2026, shows clear turquoise water washing onto a clean sandy shoreline. The right image, labelled October 2026, shows a dark band of oil contamination along the waterline, with blackened patches visible w…

blocks.text: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on Thursday that it "immediately began containment" in order to "limit environmental impacts".

Prof Steve Widdicombe, director of Sharjah Marine Science Research Centre in the UAE, told BBC Verify it was "inevitable that there will be an impact", but researchers caution it is too soon to assess extent of the damage.
Initially a much smaller oil leak could be seen emerging from the ship on 19 October.

blocks.caption: Side-by-side satellite images of a tanker at sea on 19 October. The left image, in colour, shows a dark plume trailing from the vessel and spreading into a curved slick behind it. The right radar image shows the same tanker with a long curved trail extending from its stern, indicating a leak afte…

blocks.text: But the slick appears to have rapidly spread over two days, according to radar satellite imagery reviewed by BBC Verify and intelligence firm MAIAR.

blocks.caption: Satellite image of the Gulf near the UAE coast showing a dark oil slick stretching from a leaking tanker. Annotations indicate the slick was about 35 kilometres long on 21 October. An inset map locates the incident near the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and the UAE. Source: Copernicus Sentinel-1.

blocks.text: Oil spills can cause immediate deaths of marine animals and other organisms, for example by physically trapping turtles, smothering the feathers of seabirds or damaging the gills of fish.
They can also cause longer-lasting damage, Prof Widdicombe said, if species remain exposed to toxic compounds from the oil which could impact their ability to reproduce.

Researchers have cautioned the environmental impact at this stage is very uncertain, as it depends on factors including the volume and type of oil spilled, how quickly it evaporates or breaks down and the effectiveness of the clean-up operation.

But the spill does extend towards Siniyah and Khor Al Beidah islands, a globally recognised Key Biodiversity Area containing habitats like corals, seagrasses and saltmarshes, as well as species including green turtles and the critically endangered Halavi guitarfish.
The proximity of the spill to this area is the "most concerning environmental angle", according to Eoghan Darbyshire, a scientist at the Conflict and Environment Observatory.
Tanker hit 14 days ago
BBC Verify analysis of the dimensions and location of the ship indicate they match a crude oil tanker called Gem No.2.

Maritime intelligence firm Vanguard reported the Panama-flagged tanker was "struck by an unknown projectile" on 9 October, just north of the town of Al Jazeera Al Hamra, causing a fire on board that was later extinguished.
Verified footage first posted on social media on 10 October showed the crew running across the deck and putting on lifejackets as a large cloud of black smoke rose over the ship.

blocks.caption: Three images from a ship at sea showing smoke rising on the horizon. In the left image, thick dark smoke billows into the night sky beside a vessel's deck. In the centre image, crew members wearing safety gear stand on a ship's deck as smoke rises in the distance. In the right image, a large plum…

blocks.text: Iranian state media shared footage of a ship matching Gem No.2 which appeared to show the vessel on fire with burning oil spilling into the sea.
The ship had been attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz via an "unauthorized and dangerous route", according to state media.
All 22 Indian crew members were rescued, the Indian consulate in Dubai said on 11 October.
Gem No.2 is one of a record number of ships that reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz at the start of October.

Security experts told BBC Verify this was part of an Iranian effort to assert greater control over the strait, in response to the US military successfully escorting more vessels through the vital shipping lane.
Tankers and other commercial vessels have come under attack from both Iranian and US forces in and around the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict between the two countries.
Another major oil slick washed up on the shores of Iran's Qeshm Island in August, which experts said threatened wildlife, protected ecosystems and fishing communities.
Additional reporting by Charlotte Green

articles.title: Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured
articles.summary: A shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan happened during a funeral, according to local authorities. Two unidentified men opened fire on the procession.

image.caption: Jordanian state media published surveillance video of the attack in the village of Hammoud in Karak Governorate Image: Al Mamlaka TV/AFP

blocks.text: A shooting at a church in the southern Jordanian governorate of Karak left seven people dead and another 34 wounded on Friday, Jordan's public security director Obaidallah Maaytah said.
What do we know so far?
The shooting occurred at the Hammoud Church. The shooting reportedly occurred during a funeral.
The attackers' identities and motives remain unclear. Two men opened fire on the funeral procession.

A witness told Jordanian state media there were 150 to 200 people present at the church at the time of the shooting. Videos circulating online showed wounded people on the floor of the church covered in blood, but this footage cannot be verified by DW.

Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya said a group of "extremists" carried out the massacre. According to Jordanian outlet Roya News, Al-Faraya said authorities already possess the names of suspects behind the attacks but they will not publicly disclose the identities as of now.
Jordanian government spokesperson Mohammad al-Momani said security forces have launched a probe into the attack.
Jordan King Abdullah II: 'We will strike with an iron fist'
Jordan King Abdullah II said "the terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation."

"Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity," Abdullah II said, adding, "We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation."
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, a Christian, also condemned the "heinous terrorist attack" in Jordan and expressed condolences to the victims.
US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said the news regarding the attack is "devastating."

"Praying for the victims, their families and all those affected by this depraved and brutal attack on a house of worship," Waltz said. "Attacks on Christians continue to escalate worldwide and must be stopped."
Gun attacks like the one on the church in Karak are rare in Jordan.

Although Jordan is largely a Muslim-majority country of around 11.5 million people, there is a small Christian minority of a couple hundred thousand. The Karak region, about 180 kilometers (110 miles) south of Amman, has a significant Christian population.

articles.title: Undas 2026: Bus terminals see early passenger surge for holiday exodus
articles.summary: Several passengers have started traveling to the provinces more than a week ahead of Undas, filling bus terminals early either to beat the holiday rush or to secure their tickets before the surge of…

blocks.text: Published October 23, 2026 11:20pm

Several passengers have started traveling to the provinces more than a week ahead of Undas, filling bus terminals early either to beat the holiday rush or to secure their tickets before the surge of crowds.

In a “24 Oras” report by Marisol Abdurahman on Friday, security at the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) was noticeably tighter, with baggage required to undergo inspection and scanning, while K-9 units were also deployed to check some bags.

The PITX expects passenger volume to reach up to 1.8 million from October 25 to November 4, but noted that some commuters might schedule their trips with the long weekend for the ASEAN Summit from November 16 to 18.

Several passengers queued at ticketing booths—some were buying tickets on-site, others who booked online were retrieving their boarding passes, while some found that tickets to their destinations had already sold out.
Precila Macatangay, a passenger, went to PITX early hoping to travel to Bicol immediately. However, she was only able to secure a 9 p.m. trip.
“Wala nang available. Mas maganda sana earlier para kunyari dating namin dun para umaga safe kami sa pag-uwi sa kaniya-kaniyang baloy,” Macatangay said.
(No earlier trips were available. It would have been better to leave earlier so we could arrive in the morning and safely head to our respective homes.)
Some passengers also went directly to the terminal to purchase tickets after seeing that the next available trips online were already scheduled for Sunday.
According to PITX, certain routes really fill up quickly, but they are assured that there will be enough trips for the Undas exodus.
“Makakasakay at makakasakay pa rin sila dito sa PITX dahil marami naman tayong nakaabang na additional units,” PITX spokesperson Jason Salvador said.
(They will definitely be able to get a ride here at PITX because we have plenty of additional bus units standing by.)
At the Araneta Bus Port in Cubao, Quezon City, the situation remains quiet, although some travelers have also opted to head to the provinces early for Undas.
A passenger shared that while they usually travel to their province in their private vehicle, they chose to commute this year due to high fuel prices.
“Sayang naman ‘yung gas, mas mahal sobrang mahal… Para makatipid, sakto lalo't may inaasahan na namang tataas ang presyo ng diesel sa susunod na linggo,” said Merlee Mendoza, a passenger.
(Gasoline is too expensive now... To save money, commuting makes sense, especially with another diesel price hike expected next week.)
The Araneta City Bus Port management stated that they are also expecting an influx of province-bound passengers in the coming days.
“We will be expecting ng karagdagan ding ruta. May ini-expect kaming isang operator papasok to Bicol,” Araneta City Bus Port Manager Ramon Legazpi said.
(We are expecting additional routes. We expect one operator to open trips heading to Bicol.) —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News
